deep.reconstruction:
The page is a numerical table from a geodetic adjustment, not a derivation. It belongs to the network of 21 stations (numbered 1–21; on the adjacent pages they are paired with the letters a…v, j omitted) that the previous and next pages treat with cot-formulas and complex coordinates.

Each row reads 'i.j | A(i,j) | r(i,j)':
- i.j is the line from station i to station j.
- A(i,j) is its plane azimuth (direction angle) in degrees.minutes.seconds, with seconds given to 0.001" (a decimal ',5' means 0.0005").
- r(i,j) is a number in units of 0.001".

Within each station the rows are listed in increasing azimuth (cyclically). That is the order of a round of oriented directions observed at that station.

Meaning of the right-hand column (reconstructed by me and verified on every line where both ends appear on the page):
r(i,j) = A(j,i) − 180° − A(i,j), expressed in 0.001". Consequently r(j,i) = −r(i,j).
In modern terms this is the forward/back-azimuth misclosure of each line. Each station's directions have been oriented separately, and in plane coordinates the reverse azimuth should differ from the forward one by exactly 180°. The residual measures how inconsistent the separately oriented stations are. It is the quantity such an adjustment drives to zero (or uses as the absolute term) when solving for the orientation and angle corrections δa, δab, … that appear on the neighbouring pages.

Worked examples:
- 1.2 = 1°17'40.542" and 2.1 = 181°17'40.595" give a difference of +0.053", entered as +53 and −53.
- 2.3 = 36°16'57.073" and 3.2 = 216°16'57.011" give −0.062", entered as −62 and +62.
- 3.4 gives +307 against 4.3 at −307.
- 19.20 gives −632 against 20.19 at +632.
- 18.19 gives −359.5 against 19.18 at +359.5.

All checkable pairs agree: 1-2, 2-3, 3-4, 3-5, 4-5, 4-6, 5-6, 5-7, 6-7, 6-8, 6-9, 6-10, 7-8, 8-9, 9-10, 9-11, 10-11, 10-12, 11-12, 11-13, 12-13, 12-14, 12-15, 12-16, 13-14, 14-15, 15-16, 15-17, 16-17, 16-18, 16-19, 17-18, 18-19, 18-20, 19-20, 1-20.

The lines to station 21 (1.21 −82, 2.21 +116, 3.21 −277, 4.21 +244, 19.21 +44?, 20.21 −443) cannot be checked here, because station 21's own rows are not on the page.

The network is a chain of triangles: 1-2-3-4-5-6-…-20, with node 21 tied to 1, 2, 3, 4, 19 and 20, and strong central nodes 6, 12 and 16. This matches the cyclic chain of triangles a…v on the previous page.

Context from the previous page: Gauss there states the lemma (α−β)cot C + (α−γ)cot B = (γ−β)i for the complex vertices α, β, γ of a triangle in positive order. It is correct; for example α=0, β=1, γ=i gives −1−i on both sides. That lemma expresses coordinate or azimuth changes through the angle corrections, and this table supplies the numerical misclosures for that adjustment.
